lots.title: Fire Door Specification (Lot 4 of Building Services Framework 6278)
lots.description: Supply, installation, inspection, testing, certification and maintenance of fire doors and fire door sets in properties under the control of the London Borough of Bexley. Scope includes provision of test evidence, certification, product data sheets, asset record updates, and uploading documentation to the Authority's compliance platform (TF Cloud / Civica). Document scope is broader than the parent notice lot title 'Provision of Fire Door Surveys'.
requirements: Comply with current UK Health and Safety Executive (HSE) guidance, Building Regulations, the Fire Safety Order and relevant British Standards.
Supply and install new fire doors and frames; inspect, test and certify existing fire doors; perform maintenance and remedial works to maintain compliance.
Provide all test evidence, certification, and product data sheets and update asset records.
Upload all documentation to the Authority's compliance platform (TF Cloud / Civica) for full audit trail.
Doors achieve minimum performance ratings as specified within design drawings or fire strategy documents: FD30, FD60, FD90, or FD120.
Domestic premises flat entrance doors must be a minimum FD30S rating (30 minutes fire and smoke resistance).
Intumescent and cold smoke seals must be continuous and undamaged.
Doors in corridors or staircases providing escape routes must be fitted with cold smoke brush-type seals to achieve FD30S or FD60S compliance.
All hardware must be fire-rated and tested to relevant EN standards in force, and must form part of the tested and approved door set assembly.
Self-closing devices must comply with BS EN 1154.
Fire-door hinges, compliant signage ('Fire Door - Keep Shut / Locked') and other furniture must be part of the tested approved set.
Any glazing must use fire-rated glass installed with approved fire-resistant glazing systems.
Installation must be carried out by competent installers trained in fire door installation.
All fire doors must be inspected at minimum annually; for domestic premises, communal doors must be checked quarterly per Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022.
Inspections shall include checks for leaf/frame integrity, gaps, seals, signage, and correct closer operation.
Contractors must submit installation service sheets, inspection logs, photographs and asset schedules per door, uploaded to TFCloud / Civica.
Contractors must be competent and trained in installation of fire doors, frames and door furniture; Risk Assessments and Method Statements must be approved before work begins.
On completion of any repair or installation, contractor and London Borough of Bexley representative shall carry out a joint verification inspection.
Contractor shall provide a final installation and commissioning pack including a door-by-door register and all compliance documents; non-conformances shall be rectified at contractor's cost.

Inspection shall use the Appendix A Fire Door Inspection Checklist (door leaf condition, frame condition and fixings, gaps within tolerance ≤4mm, intumescent/smoke seals continuous and undamaged, self-closer operates effectively, signage correctly fitted, no obstructions or alterations, overall Pass/Fail rating).

Asset schedule shall follow Appendix B template (Property/Block Name, Door Location, Fire Rating FD30/FD60, Door Type/Material, Installation Date, Inspection Date, Findings, Action Taken, Certification Reference).

Each install/inspection event shall be evidenced by a certificate following the Appendix C example (Certificate No, Door ID, Location, Installer, Date Installed, Fire Rating, Smoke Seal Yes/No, Inspector Signature, Date of Inspection).

warnings.message: This document is a draft technical specification only and contains no evaluation criteria, scoring weights or award methodology. Evaluation criteria array is empty. They likely live in a separate ITT / SQ / award-criteria document not provided to this run.

Notice-level lot 4 title is 'Provision of Fire Door Surveys' but this specification covers supply, installation, inspection, certification, and maintenance of fire doors and fire door sets. Document scope is broader than the parent notice lot title; notice metadata may understate the lot.

The specification document does not cite CPV codes directly. Lot CPV (50700000-2 – Repair and maintenance services of building installations) is inherited from the parent notice metadata; product seed CPVs (44221220-3 fire doors, 44521120-5 emergency-exit / closer hardware) are heuristic candidates derived from product wording, not from explicit document citation. Treat with low confidence.

The hardware/ironmongery sub-section (§3.3) renders without sentence terminators between 'Hinges', the 'Compliant signage' clause, and the assembly-conformance clause. Requirements were split semantically but original sentence boundaries are uncertain.

Document title indicates a draft specification ('6278 - Draft Specification - Lot 4'). Final published version may differ; downstream consumers should reconcile against the final ITT pack when available.
